title: Deploy the access-request (RFA) broker
purpose: Deploys the public access-request (RFA) broker of PIM Manager Pro: its storage account and tables, its network, its Container Apps environment and app, the storage rights and Easy Auth; with the inputs given it also registers the API audience, the broker's mail sender and PIM's RFA settings. Plan only unless -Apply.
whenToRun: After the main installation, when the access-request portal (Pro add-on) is wanted. The broker is always public by design (an internal environment is refused); -ApiAllowedIps restricts it to known systems. Placement Shared puts it in its own subnet of the PIM VNet; Island in its own subscription. It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Deploy-PimRfaBroker.ps1). When the store's SQL server is private, run it from inside the network so the settings step can reach it.

runAs.name: Owner (or Contributor + User Access Administrator)
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (Shared) or the RFA subscription (Island)
runAs.why: Creates the storage account, tables, NSG, subnet, Container Apps environment, Log Analytics workspace and app, and assigns Storage Table Data Contributor on the storage account.

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.why: Adds the broker's subnet (delegated to Microsoft.App/environments) and its NSG.

runAs.name: Application Administrator
runAs.scope: the tenant (only with -TenantId: the API audience follow-up)
runAs.why: Set-PimRfaBrokerApiAuth.ps1 registers the 'PIM access request API' app so Entra application tokens are accepted.

runAs.name: Admin application with Exchange.ManageAsApp (-AdminAppId + -AdminCertThumbprint), only for the mail follow-up
runAs.why: Initialize-PimMailSender.ps1 scopes the broker identity's send right to the sender mailbox; Exchange RBAC needs an application identity. Without it the step is printed as NEXT.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins) via -UseSignedInAccount, or the admin application
runAs.scope: the environment's SQL database (only with -SqlServerFqdn: the settings follow-up)
runAs.why: Writes pim.Settings RfaSettings and switches the rfa.portal and api.broker feature gates on.

changes.target: Azure (PIM resource group or RFA subscription)
changes.object: storage account (Tables; shared-key access disabled, TLS 1.2, no public blob) and the RFA tables
changes.why: The broker's only data store: requests, reviews, PINs, API keys.

changes.object: NSG nsg-<app> (deny to the PIM subnets) and the broker subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments (Shared), or its own VNet (Island)
changes.scope: the PIM VNet or the RFA subscription
changes.why: The broker is isolated from PIM's own subnets.
changes.undo: Delete the subnet and the NSG (Island: the VNet).

changes.object: the public Container Apps environment (with a Log Analytics workspace beside it) and the container app ca-pim-rfa with a system-assigned identity
changes.why: Runs the broker (the PIM image, scale to zero by default).
changes.undo: Delete the container app, the environment and the workspace.

changes.object: the broker app's identity and each engine identity (-EngineIdentityPrincipalIds)
changes.why: The broker writes requests; the engine pulls them. It is the broker's ONLY Azure right.

changes.object: Easy Auth (Entra provider, unauthenticated = allow) and, with -ApiAllowedIps, the ingress allow-list
changes.why: The portal is PIN-based; /api/v1 needs a validated token or an API key. The allow-list makes the whole broker non-public.
changes.undo: Disable Easy Auth / remove the ingress rules.

changes.object: the 'PIM access request API' app registration (Set-PimRfaBrokerApiAuth.ps1)
changes.why: So Entra application tokens are accepted on the API.

changes.target: Exchange Online (only with the admin application)
changes.permission: send as the sender mailbox only (Exchange-scoped application RBAC, Initialize-PimMailSender.ps1)
changes.why: The broker mails PINs and decisions.
changes.undo: Remove the management role assignment and scope (see Initialize-PimMailSender).

changes.object: pim.Settings RfaSettings (store + portal URL, existing API app ids kept) and FeatureGates (rfa.portal + api.broker ON)
changes.why: Tells PIM where the broker is; read back.
changes.undo: Manager > Settings > RFA broker & API: clear the store, and switch the two gates off.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The PIM subscription (GUID).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The PIM resource group.

parameters.name: Placement
parameters.help: Shared (own subnet in the PIM VNet) or Island (own subscription, own VNet, not peered).

parameters.name: RfaSubscriptionId
parameters.help: Island: the broker's own subscription (must differ from PIM's).

parameters.name: RfaResourceGroup
parameters.help: Island: the broker's resource group.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: The Azure region.

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: Shared: the PIM VNet (the broker gets its own subnet there). Island: its own VNet (default vnet-pim-rfa).

parameters.name: SubnetName
parameters.help: The broker subnet's name.

parameters.name: SubnetPrefix
parameters.help: The broker subnet, an IPv4 CIDR of /27 or larger.

parameters.name: PimSubnetPrefixes
parameters.help: Shared: the PIM subnet prefixes the broker subnet's NSG denies traffic to.

parameters.name: StorageAccountName
parameters.help: The broker's storage account (3-24 lower-case letters / digits).

parameters.name: EnvironmentName
parameters.help: The broker's Container Apps environment.

parameters.name: AppName
parameters.help: The broker's container app.

parameters.name: Image
parameters.help: The PIM Manager image (same as the jobs), e.g. <registry>.azurecr.io/pim-manager@sha256:<digest>.

parameters.name: AcrName
parameters.help: The registry name, pulled with the app's system identity.

parameters.name: SenderMailbox
parameters.help: The PIM mail sender the broker sends as.

parameters.name: TenantName
parameters.help: The tenant name shown on the portal.

parameters.name: EngineIdentityPrincipalIds
parameters.help: The engine (tick job) managed identity object id(s): they pull the requests from the store.

parameters.name: ApiAllowedIps
parameters.help: Allow ingress only from these IPv4 addresses / CIDRs (the API-only shape: the portal is then not public).

parameters.name: MinReplicas
parameters.help: 0 (scale to zero) .. 2; 1 keeps one warm.

parameters.name: ExistingEnvironmentName
parameters.help: Shared only: join an existing PUBLIC Container Apps environment instead of building one.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: Pins the sign-in to the PIM tenant; also runs the API audience follow-up.

parameters.name: ApiAppDisplayName
parameters.help: The API app registration's name.

parameters.name: AzureConfigDir
parameters.help: Ignored (the script no longer uses the Azure CLI); kept so older command lines still run.

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Admin application (client) id for the mail and settings follow-ups (with -AdminCertThumbprint).

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Thumbprint of the admin application's certificate in the local machine store.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: The settings follow-up writes the store as the signed-in person (a member of the SQL admin group).

parameters.name: SqlServerFqdn
parameters.help: The store's SQL server: runs the settings follow-up.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.help: The database.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Run the steps. Without it the plan is printed only.

readsOnly: the storage account, VNet, NSG, subnet, Container Apps environment and app (each step creates only what is missing)
the existing role assignments on the storage account
pim.Settings RfaSettings and FeatureGates (settings follow-up, before writing)
whatIf:
Validates the inputs and prints 'What if: Performing the operation "deploy step(s)" on target " RFA broker in "' and the numbered plan ('RFA broker deploy -- placement

-- PLAN ONLY'). -WhatIf wins over -Apply; no step runs and nothing is signed in to.
undo: Delete the broker's container app, Container Apps environment, Log Analytics workspace, storage account, subnet and NSG (Island: the resource group), the 'PIM access request API' app registration and the broker's Exchange send scope; clear RfaSettings and switch rfa.portal / api.broker off in the Manager.
